EDS AI Workflow (Eitri Agentic Dev Workflow)

Path to production

Code changes pass through four pipeline stages on their way to production. Each stage widens the scope of the checks, from the developer’s staged change at commit time to the whole codebase at QA entry and before release. The same skills are reused at each scope, so enforcement stays consistent without duplicate tooling.

This page is for Tech Leads, reviewers and the team that maintains the pipeline. It starts where the developer harness closeout ends and finishes with the consolidated report for the Tech Lead’s release sign-off. Confirm the applicable release authority locally.

Follow the four pipeline stages

Read the stages from left to right. A commit triggers checks on the staged diff only. A merge request to Dev generates documentation for the changed files. A merge request to QA runs full-codebase scans and generators. Promoting a release candidate runs every readiness gate again on the full codebase and produces one report for the Tech Lead.

Pipeline stages, triggers, skills, scope and blocking behaviour
StageTriggerSkillsScopeBlocking
4.1 Pre-commitHusky pre-commit hook/code-reviewer, which includes /im8-reviewStaged diffBlocks the commit on Critical or High findings
4.2 Merge to DevMR targeting the Dev branch/gen-code-docsMR diffPass-through
4.3 Merge to QAMR targeting the QA branch/im8-review, /gen-auth-matrix, /tech-arch-doc, /dependency-vuln-scan, /semgrepFull codebaseScanners block on Critical or High; generators pass through
4.4 Pre-productionRelease candidate promotion/pre-prod-check, which runs every readiness gateFull codebaseBlocks the release on any gate failure

Source: [1] section 4.

4.1 Check each commit

A Husky pre-commit hook runs /code-reviewer on the staged diff whenever a developer runs git commit. It is the same validation gate used inside /do-work (Gate 2), scoped to the staged changes for fast feedback. It dispatches the two-axis /code-review, /semgrep static analysis, the /im8-review security audit, /thermo-nuclear-review and the framework reviews in parallel.

  • Gate behaviour: blocks the commit on any Critical or High finding. The harness allows --no-verify to bypass the hook in an emergency.
  • Output: a consolidated report at artifacts/code-reviewer/{slug}-compliance.html.

The IM8 review checks application technical controls such as input validation, authentication, secrets management, Content Security Policy (CSP), session management and audit logging.

Sources: [1] section 4.1; [2] Implementation skills.

4.2 Document changes when merging to Dev

A merge request to the Dev branch triggers /gen-code-docs on the changed files only, giving reviewers quick API documentation diffs. It detects the stack from tsconfig.json, pom.xml or Gradle build files and generates documentation for each stack present: TypeDoc output in docs/tsdoc/ and Javadoc output in docs/javadoc/, both from inline comments.

This stage is pass-through: documentation generation does not block the merge. Full-codebase documentation is generated at pre-production.

Source: [1] section 4.2.

4.3 Scan the full codebase when merging to QA

A merge request to the QA branch runs full-codebase security scans and documentation generators. Their outputs support threat and risk analysis and technical documentation sign-off.

Checks at the merge to QA
SkillWhat it doesOutputGate
/im8-reviewReviews all code against IM8 application technical controls for Spring Boot and React with TypeScript.A summary table and a PASS, FAIL, WARN or N/A finding per control, with file paths and line numbersBlocks on Critical or High
/gen-auth-matrixExtracts access rules from the OpenAPI specification and maps each role to the endpoints and resources it can reach. Needs an OpenAPI specification, such as one from springdoc-openapi.checklists/auth-matrix-{timestamp}.html, security schemes, and endpoints without authorisation flagged as potential gapsPass-through
/tech-arch-docDeep-scans every module and the dependency manifests, then runs /dependency-vuln-scan.docs/tech-architecture.md and .html: system overview, module catalogue, technology decisions linked to ADRs, database design, dependency inventory with licences, and vulnerability findingsPass-through
/dependency-vuln-scanRuns npm audit or yarn audit for Node, and the OWASP Dependency-Check plugin for Maven or Gradle.CVE counts by severity, findings per package, upgrade commands for Critical and High findings, and scanner notesBlocks on Critical or High CVEs
/semgrepRuns the p/security-audit and p/default rulesets: injection, insecure deserialisation, weak cryptography, hard-coded secrets, unsafe input handling and dangerous dependency patterns.Must-fix findings (P0, P1) in code the current task created, modified or made worse; documented findings (P2) in unrelated existing codeBlocks on Critical or High

All outputs are point-in-time. Re-run the generators after codebase or dependency changes.

Source: [1] section 4.3.

4.4 Confirm pre-production readiness

Before promoting a release candidate, run /pre-prod-check. It runs every readiness gate in sequence on the full codebase and writes one sign-off report for the Tech Lead. You can also run any gate on its own to recheck it without the full suite.

  1. /gen-code-docs generates TypeDoc and Javadoc API documentation.
  2. /gen-auth-matrix generates the authorisation matrix.
  3. /owasp-threat-modeling produces the threat model for review.
  4. /tech-arch-doc generates the technical architecture document, running /dependency-vuln-scan internally.
  5. /im8-review checks the full codebase against IM8 controls.
  6. /spring-logging-review checks observability readiness.
  7. /semgrep audits secrets and configuration.
  8. The skill writes a consolidated sign-off report for the Tech Lead’s review.

Most of these gates also ran at earlier stages; here they run again to give a definitive audit at release time. Two are pre-production only:

  • Threat modelling, /owasp-threat-modeling: models the system as data-flow diagrams in OWASP Threat Dragon, identifies threats with STRIDE, adding LINDDUN for privacy-sensitive features, and triages each as Mitigated, Not Applicable or Open, with mitigations for every Open item. It produces a PDF and a JSON model kept in version control; update it when the architecture changes. Threat Dragon must be installed, through Docker or the desktop app.
  • Observability, /spring-logging-review: checks SLF4J usage, log levels, exception logging, sensitive-data and personal-data leakage, log injection, MDC and correlation IDs across asynchronous boundaries, structured output and production logging configuration. It reports findings with file paths and suggests corrected code.

Note

/im8-review checks IM8 controls in the code. ARC controls are assessed against the TRD by /spec-compliance at Step 8; the harness documentation does not describe a code-level ARC check. Do not read the pre-production report as evidence of ARC compliance in the code.

Sources: [1] section 4.4; [2] Path to production skills.

Plan what happens after readiness

The pipeline gates establish readiness for release, not the rollout itself. Plan limited exposure, observation and recovery, and feed production evidence back into the next PRD, using the Release and observe and Learn stages in Product implementation.

Source: [3] sections 4.5 and 4.6.

Definition of done for the pipeline and pre-production

Pipeline gates are done (stages 4.1–4.3) when

  • Pre-commit: /code-reviewer, including /im8-review, reports no Critical or High findings on the staged diff.
  • Merge to Dev: API documentation is generated for the changed files with /gen-code-docs.
  • Merge to QA: /im8-review reports no Critical or High findings on the full codebase.
  • Merge to QA: the authorisation matrix is generated with /gen-auth-matrix.
  • Merge to QA: the technical architecture document is generated with /tech-arch-doc.
  • Merge to QA: /dependency-vuln-scan finds no Critical or High CVEs.
  • Merge to QA: /semgrep reports no Critical or High security findings.

Pre-production is done (stage 4.4) when

  • API documentation is generated with /gen-code-docs.
  • The authorisation matrix is generated and reviewed, including any endpoints flagged as unprotected.
  • The threat model is reviewed and all findings are triaged with /owasp-threat-modeling.
  • The technical architecture document is generated with /tech-arch-doc.
  • No Critical or High CVEs remain unmitigated.
  • Full-codebase IM8 compliance is confirmed with /im8-review.
  • Observability readiness is confirmed with /spring-logging-review.
  • /semgrep reports no critical security findings.
  • The consolidated report from /pre-prod-check is approved by the Tech Lead.

Next step: check which of these stages your pipeline already enforces, and agree with your platform team how the missing ones will be added. To change what each stage checks against, add your team’s context.

Sources: [1] sections 3 and 4.4.
